license.notes: Zoo 1.77.0. The fence at the playable edge: the walker, 2026-10-04, on the fenced vacant lot in docs/findings/backdrop_mock/ -- 'I like the idea of a fence between playable areas and non playable areas, thats good feedback to the player'. REFERENCE: a commercial chain-link fence (ASTM F1043 framework, F668/F392 fabric): galvanised line posts 1-7/8 in OD no more than 10 ft apart, 2-3/8 in terminal posts at the ends, a 1-5/8 in top rail through the line posts' loop caps, 2 in mesh fabric hung 2 in above grade with a tension wire along its bottom; 6 ft fabric is the commercial default. Planned in core/chain_link_fence_forms.py. TWO SUBMISSIONS whatever the length: the steel (posts, rail, wire: one mesh in metal_bare) and the fabric (one card in Pixelcoat's chain_link, an alpha-cut 1 m tile of 16 diamonds, read from both sides). Width is the run's length and depth is exactly a terminal post's diameter, so the slot is what stands; collision is that box, a wall nobody walks through and everybody sees through. Height is the fabric's, 4 to 8 ft.
